cards.card_text: And here's what they proclaim, the very last line: "The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness." That's a tree I'd park my gold base right next to, friend.
cards.verse_text: to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.”
cards.snippet: …is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.”

cards.card_text: Then the LORD calls out a woe on the man who builds his palace by unrighteousness and his upper rooms without justice.
cards.verse_text: “Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness, and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his countrymen serve without pay, and fails to pay their wages,

cards.card_text: If our unrighteousness highlights God's righteousness, is God unjust to bring His wrath on us?
cards.verse_text: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say?
cards.snippet: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say?

cards.card_text: The writer wraps up the thought: "All unrighteousness is sin, yet there is sin that does not lead to death."
